A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PGCM research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, prototype-editing experiments, concept-intervention curves, and a prototype-count analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds CUB evaluations, noisy-CLEVR-Hans3 editing experiments, and downstream task-intervention results.

M1.justification: The core PGCM architecture and inference procedure remain. For the added CUB experiment, Appendix B introduces an adaptation that operates on and reconstructs ResNet18 embeddings instead of image pixels. Appendix A.1 specifies cosine similarity with temperature 25 for CUB, while retaining dot products for the original datasets.

E1.justification: v2 adds CUB bird classification with bird-attribute concepts and extends noisy-label evaluation to CLEVR-Hans3. CelebAMask-HQ is a clarified dataset name, since v1 already describes using CelebA-HQ masks; CLEVR-Hans3 likewise already appears in v1.

E2.justification: DNN, CBM, CRM, and CMR remain the accuracy comparators, and intervention comparisons retain CBM, CRM, and CMR. Extending these comparisons to CUB does not change comparator membership. v2 explicitly explains the absence of CLEVR-Hans comparisons, which were also absent from v1.

E3.justification: The added CUB evaluation introduces a substantial protocol: 200-epoch ResNet18 fine-tuning, shared extracted embeddings for PGCM and competitors, whole-image inputs without segmentation, and 350 prototypes. Existing benchmark metrics and training settings are retained. The joint versus pretrained segmentation descriptions add documentation rather than establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v1 plots concept accuracy after interventions; v2 additionally tests downstream task accuracy across ColorMNIST+, CUB, and CelebA in Appendix D, Figure 6. It also adds CUB concept-intervention analysis and extends prototype-removal/editing tests to noisy CLEVR-Hans3. The prototype-count ablation and earlier qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 1, 2, and 3 and use the same plus/minus summaries and shaded-curve reporting. v2 introduces no changed run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds CUB results, including PGCM concept/task accuracies of 90.0±0.1/63.4±0.9, and CLEVR-Hans3 editing results improving from 81.6±0.4 to 95.1±3.1 after removal or 97.5±1.0 after editing. New intervention curves report additional outcomes, and Figure 4 revises the CelebA PGCM/PGCM* curves. Original ColorMNIST+ and CelebA accuracy-table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The graphical assumptions, probabilistic definitions, concept-semantics equation, Appendix C ELBO derivation, and Appendix A.3 complexity expressions remain substantively unchanged. Equation renumbering and delimiter corrections do not add mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims remain verifiable visual concept grounding, prototype-level intervention, and competitive predictive accuracy. The abstract changes 'match' to 'achieve similar' performance without materially changing that claim; the additional experiments support the existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges dependence on segmentation quality and the risk of interventions incorrectly affecting other concepts. Appendix D adds interpretations connecting task responsiveness to sidechannels and concept correlations, and explains the missing CLEVR-Hans baseline evaluation. The existing capacity–interpretability tradeoff remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, detailed CUB fine-tuning settings, CUB prototype configuration, per-dataset training times, a 150-hour experiment estimate, and dataset-license information. It also clarifies segmentation training and corrects Appendix A.2's prototype-matching description from f_concept(e_j) to e_j. Existing hardware and seed disclosures were already present.

R1.justification: Related work adds Wang et al.'s Align2concept and distinguishes PGCM's predefined concepts from concept-discovery approaches by Knab et al. and Prasse et al. Lee et al. is added for the facial-mask dataset. These are focused additions within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain. v2 refines explanations, removes the informal model-checking analogy, condenses the research questions, reorders experimental findings, and revises the conclusion with limitations and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and repositioning material. Accuracy and editing tables are expanded and reordered; Figure 4 gains a CUB panel and shared legend; task-intervention Figure 6 is added. Existing appendix illustrations are retained but regrouped.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the intervention claims: v1 mainly measures concept correction, whereas the new task-intervention curves directly test downstream benefits and reveal the weak or adverse CelebA regime. CUB comparisons and noisy-CLEVR editing broaden this evidence, while added implementation information and explicit limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. The CUB embedding adaptation and unspecified CLEVR noise-generation recipe limit the reach and reproducibility of the additions.
